issues.description: Command names use plural form inconsistent with sibling singular convention.
issues.detail: Existing commands are quickmark_save, quickmark_load, bookmark_add, bookmark_load (singular). New commands use quickmarks_reload and bookmarks_reload, breaking the convention in three places (commands.py and both feature scenarios). Rename to quickmark_reload and bookmark_reload to match the file's voice and preserve tab-completion discoverability.

issues.description: reload() is non-atomic: clears marks before parsing, leaving empty/partial state on failure.
issues.detail: self.marks.clear() runs before the new file is read and parsed. If _init_lineparser fails or _parse_line raises on a malformed line mid-iteration, the user is left with empty or partially-loaded marks while the UI reports success. Build a local OrderedDict from disk first, then swap atomically and emit changed only on success.

issues.description: reload() silently swallows parse errors with no user feedback distinguishing success from partial failure.
issues.detail: In __init__, parse errors surfaced at startup. At runtime via the new command, errors raised mid-iteration produce no distinct user feedback — the 'reloaded' message shows even when a malformed line aborted iteration. Make error handling explicit and surface failure to the user.

issues.description: Unit test does not cover the failure mode or assert old entries are cleared.
issues.detail: test_reload exercises only the happy path. It never asserts the prior entry (http://example.com) is gone after reload — the whole point of clearing self.marks — and never tests a malformed line on reload, which would catch the partial-mutation bug. Add a negative test and an assertion that removed entries disappear.

issues.description: New BDD scenarios are unnamed and only assert the success message, not behavior.
issues.detail: Both new Gherkin scenarios use bare `Scenario:` while every other scenario in the file is titled, hurting grep-ability and failure output. They also only assert the status message, not that the file was actually re-read. Add titles and assert a newly-written entry is present after reload.

issues.description: Extract a pure _load_marks helper to separate parsing from identity mutation.
issues.detail: The parse loop (skip blanks/comments, _parse_line) is duplicated conceptually between __init__ flow and reload(). A pure `_load_marks(lineparser) -> OrderedDict` separates the value (parsed marks) from the identity update (assign + emit). Both __init__ and reload would call it, reducing complecting and enabling the atomic swap above.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the refactor's intent — extracting reload() so it runs at both startup and on a user command — is sound, but the implementation has real correctness and consistency issues. Most critically, reload() clears in-memory marks before reading disk, so any parse failure leaves users with empty/partial state while the UI reports success. Command names (quickmarks_reload, bookmarks_reload) violate the file's singular-noun convention used by every sibling command. Tests cover only the happy path and the new BDD scenarios are unnamed. Fix the naming, make reload atomic via a local-build-then-swap, surface parse errors to the user, and tighten the tests before merge.
